Items.Authors: Lorenzo Ferrari Barusso, Flavio Gatti, Edvige Celasco, Manuela Rigano, Daniele Brienza, Elisabetta Cavazzuti, Gabriele Minervini, Giacomo Gorla, Matteo D'Andrea, Claudio Macculi
Items.Title: Methods on the TRL-5 assessment for the production of the CryoAC chip for X-IFU newAthena
Items.Abstract: The Cryogenic Anti-Coincidence detector (CryoAC) is a key subsystem of the newAthena X-IFU, designed to reduce cosmic-ray–induced background in the TES array. This work outlines the development of the fabrication processes and product-assurance activities required to meet ESA standards for space instrumentation. After validating the procedures, a batch of Demonstration Models (DM 1.2) was produced. The fabrication effort focuses on precise superconducting film transitions, reliable microfabrication, and strict environmental control. Complementary product-assurance activities include repeatability checks, vibration tests, and verification of procedural clarity. The results provide a roadmap for the future production and qualification of CryoAC units, emphasizing the importance of manufacturing accuracy and rigorous quality assurance coordinated by ASI.

Items.Authors: Felix C. M. Bettonvil, Chad Salo, Sander Kwast, Jeff Lynn
Items.Title: METIS risk management
Items.Abstract: The Mid-infrared ELT Imager and Spectrograph (METIS) is one of the four first-generation scientific instruments for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). METIS, designed to operate in the mid-infrared wavelength range, aims at both imaging, spectroscopy and coronagraphy. METIS is now in its manufacturing, assembly, integration and test phase (MAIT), and started recently the System AIT phase. The METIS project is of a substantially bigger scale than previous VLT projects, but still smaller than space missions. In this paper we present the risk management of METIS, both in terms of strategy, decision taking, costing and lessons learned.

Items.Authors: Henk J. van Weers
Items.Title: Micro-vibration test-program of the X-IFU focal plane assembly development model 1.1
Items.Abstract: This work describes the micro-vibration measurement setup realized for the XIFU Focal Plane Assembly Development Model 1.1 (FPA DM1.1). It shows an approach based on measurement of the rigid body motion at the FPA interfaces. This with the purpose to overcome the high modal density of mechanical resonances present in the commercial cryogenic test bed in the frequency range of interest. These rigid body motions are also compared to the responses predicted by Finite Element Modelling (FEM). The micro-shaker units are developed in house and optimized for cryogenic use within the 40 Hz to 1 kHz range.

Items.Authors: María Concepción Cárdenas Vázquez, Armin Huber, Thomas Bertram, Peter Bizenberger, Daniel J. Ahrer, Ralf-Rainer Rohloff, Silvia Scheithauer
Items.Title: MITESI, Mini-ELT Telescope Simulator: from the concept to the real hardware in the lab
Items.Abstract: MITESI, Mini elt TElescope SImulator, is a project to produce a hardware and software system designed to test and verify ELT instrument requirements in the laboratory before on-telescope deployment.   Its first application is the performance verification of the METIS Single Conjugate Adaptive Optics (SCAO) subsystem at the Max Planck Institute for Astronomy. It combines an opto-mechanical setup with advanced features for adaptive optics testing, including a deformable mirror, a diffraction-limited light source, and a real-time post-DM image monitoring system. It is capable of reproducing key ELT characteristics—such as atmospheric wavefronts, an ELT-shaped pupil, 1–4 µm broadband operation, a wide field of view, and an M5 simulator.  The system is currently in the assembly and integration phase and will soon transition to validation. This contribution outlines its requirements, implemented functionalities, final optical and opto-mechanical designs, and associated tolerance analysis.

Items.Authors: Giacomo Cherchi, Nicolas Gorius, Fabrizio Cogato, Isabella Pagano, Gianalfredo Nicolini, Elisabetta Tommasi Di Vignano
Items.Title: Mitigation of the line start effect in PLATO normal camera CCDs for accurate read-out noise characterization
Items.Abstract: PLATO is ESA's M3 mission to detect and characterise exoplanets around bright solar-type stars using high-precision space photometry. The payload includes 26 cameras: 24 Normal Cameras (N-CAMs) for photometry and 2 Fast Cameras for bright targets and guidance. Each N-CAM hosts four CCDs, each read out on two sides. During thermal-vacuum tests, bias and dark frames are acquired to characterise the read-out noise (RON) of each side. The CCD bias exhibits a Line Start Effect (LSE), a column-dependent offset at line start that leads to a systematic overestimation of pixel-to-pixel noise and can cause RON to exceed its requirement. For each side, an LSE profile is derived by averaging bias frames along rows and subtracted before recomputing RON maps. After presenting the general framework and the analysis concept, in this presentation, we show how the LSE mitigation reducing high-noise tails and restoring compliance with the N-CAM noise requirement.

Items.Authors: Oisín O. Creaner, Cáthal McAleer, Gerhard Ulbricht, Gary Donegan, Colm Bracken, Mario de Lucia, Tom Ray
Items.Title: MKID simulation through automated geometry generation
Items.Abstract: We present a software package to generate geometry models of Microwave Kinetic Inductance Detectors (MKIDs) at scale. Through a graphical user interface (GUI), the user can set resonator parameters such as inductor and capacitor dimensions. They can also adjust the granularity of the simulation and introduce non-ideal artefacts of the lithographic process such as rounding of corners or edge irregularly. The software will then iteratively generate geometry files matching those parameters. By inputting these files to established simulation software, it is possible to simulate large numbers of MKIDs under both idealised and non-ideal conditions. This software thus enables MKIDs development teams to rapidly iterate their designs in silico while including more realistic allowances for fabrication tolerance.

Items.Authors: Alessio Taranto, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Luca Rosignoli, Elana Urbach, Fritz Mueller, Aashay Pai, Eli Rykoff, Alex Drlica-Wagner, Hannah M. M. Pollek, John Andrew, Douglas R. Neill, Parker Fagrelius, Tomislav Vicuna, Christopher W. Stubbs, Robert H. Lupton, Travis Lange, Andrew P. Rasmussen, Aaron Roodman, Chuck F. Claver, Joshua E. Meyers, Anastasia Alexov, Keith Bechtol, Lee S. Kelvin, Lynne R. Jones, Brian Stalder, Leanne Guy, Tiago Ribeiro, Erik Dennihy, Bruno C. Quint, Aaron Emery Watkins, Alysha Shugart, Lukas Eisert, Kevin Fanning, Marina Pavlović, Yijung Kang, Hye Yun Park, Paulo Lago, Kris Mortensen, Paulina Venegas, Minhee Hyun, Karla Peña, David Sanmartim, Qianjun Hang, Gonzalo Aravena, Kshitija Kelkar, Kate Napier, Jacqueline Seron, Carlos Morales, Danica Žilková, Eric Christensen, Yusra Alsayyad, William O'Mullane, Enrico Giro, Rodolfo Canestrari, Sandrine Thomas, Kevin Reil, Claudio H. Araya Cortes, Roberto Tighe, Holger Drass, Pablo Zorzi, Massimo Brescia
Items.Title: Modeling of the diffuse background produced by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory M2 baffle scattered light
Items.Abstract: The secondary mirror (M2) cell baffle on the Simonyi Telescope restricts the light that reaches the LSSTCam focal plane thereby also shaping the inner edge of the telescope optical pupil. This work studies the contribution to the background of the residual light scattered by the M2 baffle when illuminated by highly off-axis light beams. The study is based on in-dome, multi-wavelength testing using a Collimated Beam Projector (CBP), currently in use for calibration purposes, and ray-tracing simulations to retro-fit the test data to an on-sky scenario. These simulations infer the intensity and spatial distribution of background scattered light within the different LSSTCam filters for different star asterism and spectral stellar classes.

Items.Authors: Riccardo Campana
Items.Title: Modeling proton-induced activation background in high energy space instrumentation
Items.Abstract: Proton-induced activation is a major background source for high-energy missions in low-Earth orbit, where trapped protons create radioactive isotopes that degrade sensitivity. Full Monte Carlo simulations are inefficient due to rare isotope production and the large number of decay events required. We review a fast, modular framework that reconstructs activation backgrounds by separating isotope production, decay evolution, and detector-response synthesis. Production yields come from monochromatic proton Geant4 runs, decay activities from Bateman-equation solutions, and background from simulated isotope emissions. The method reduces computational cost by orders of magnitude while retaining the accuracy of direct simulations. We present applications to HERMES, eXTP (LAD/WFM), and THESEUS/XGIS demonstrate its versatility and its value for rapidly assessing design and operational choices in future high-energy missions.

Items.Authors: Peter J. Young
Items.Title: Modernising GHOST’s Image Display: From JSky to a Pure JavaFX Implementation
Items.Abstract: The GHOST GUI, a Java-based interface for astronomical observations, originally used JSky, a Swing-based image display library developed by ESO and adopted by Gemini for their Observing Tool. Integration via SwingNode limited performance, as JSky depends on the outdated Java Advanced Imaging (JAI) library and does not exploit modern GPU acceleration.  To resolve these limitations, a new image display component, JavaFXImageViewer, was developed entirely in JavaFX. Early prototypes demonstrated substantial performance improvements, leading to a full replacement of the legacy JSky component. Development productivity was enhanced through the use of AI-assisted programming tools, which supported code generation, refactoring, and design exploration.  The new library has recently been commissioned, achieving up to 75× faster rendering of 6k × 6k images on a MacBook M2 Pro and up to 20× faster on a 32-core Intel Xeon server (without GPU).

Items.Authors: Florian Quatresooz, Kyliann Robert, Yoshimi Rokugawa, Kenta Sakabe, Kenta Nakamura, Yuma Abe, Cyril Petit, Aurélie Bonnefois, Gaël Kermarrec, David Alaluf, Nicolas Védrenne
Items.Title: Monitoring atmospheric turbulence from stellar observations at optical ground stations
Items.Abstract: Many optical ground stations (OGSs) deployed for free-space optical communications now include adaptive optics (AO), offering the opportunity to retrieve optical turbulence profiles from AO telemetry. At ONERA’s FEELINGS OGS near Toulouse, we recently demonstrated real-time estimation of Cn2 and wind profiles during satellite links. However, limited by the availability of satellites, we explore whether our approach can utilize stellar sources in the infrared instead of satellite downlinks. This raises challenges in exposure time, noise handling, and estimation accuracy, first studied in simulations and with laboratory experiments. We also extend our methodology to NICT’s 1-m OGS in Tokyo, paving the way for routine, multi-site turbulence monitoring using stellar observations.

Items.Authors: Ludovico Teodori, Paolo Ciliegi, Andrea Di Rocco, Marco Riva, Demetrio Magrin, Lorenzo Busoni, Simonetta Chinellato, Jacopo Farinato, Italo Foppiani, Gianluca Di Rico, Vincenzo De Caprio, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Gabriele Umbriaco
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT : Procurement governance and gating strategy during the Final Design Phase
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope, providing MCAO correction for MICADO and HARMONI. In MORFEO, procurement is a key element of Phase C (Final Design Phase) , where acquisition processes evolve with design maturity. Tender packages are released progressively, according to subsystem readiness and consolidated requirements and interfaces. Intermediate reviews, conducted with ESO, validate the completeness of each tender package and authorize early procurement of long-lead items, once parameters reach sufficient maturity. Early procurement mitigates schedule exposure but does not authorize fabrication, which will begin only after the Final Design Review. The contribution focuses on MORFEO’s procurement approach, outlining how early acquisition in Phase C and integrated design-to-manufacturing tenders contribute to system coherence and risk reduction.

Items.Authors: MAHSHID SHIRI, Enrico Cascone, Christian Eredia, vincenzo cianniello, Vincenzo Dellacorte, Mirko colapietro, Sergio D'Orsi, Mina Sibalic, Manca Francesco, Jacopo farinato
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: development and experimental validation of a modular motion control architecture for the MORFEO instrument of the ELT
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay for ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.  The paper describes the design and experimental validation of modular motion and instrument control architecture developed for the mechanical subsystems of MORFEO. The architecture is designed for compliance with ESO standards, including strict component selection guided by ESO to ensure enhanced maintainability, scalability, and interoperability with the ELT control system. It describes the adopted methodology for the validation of the design against stringent performance requirements, such as consistency of operation and stability of real-time communication. It also gives an overview of the most important features in the implementation on a dedicated test bench and then demonstrates how the system can ensure operational reliability for MORFEO functions.

Items.Authors: Christian Eredia, Mahshid Shiri, Vincenzo Cianniello, Enrico Cascone
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: general overview of the instrument control hardware design towards the final design review
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.  This paper shows the evolution of the Instrument Control Hardware design of MORFEO, as it approaches the Final Design Review milestone. The design is developed to harmonise compliance with ESO standards, based on industrial paradigms such as PLC and fieldbus protocol, and the specific needs of the system.  In particular, a description of the main aspects and challenges of the design is given, including choice of electronics cabinet standard and of their internal layout, overall distribution of the various types of network that are available at the ELT, characterisation of the mirrors tip-tilt motorised functions, routing strategy, with a focus on the major developments in the last two years of the project.

Items.Authors: Giuseppe De Luca, Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli, Tommaso Lapucci, Marco Bonaglia
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: LOR anti-collision system design and test validation
Items.Abstract: The Low Order Reconstructor (LOR) of MORFEO, the multi‑conjugate adaptive optics relay for the ELT, incorporates three axisymmetric optical benches equipped with pick‑off mirrors to track guide stars. The system geometry introduces potential collisions between arms and adjacent structures, requiring protective measures. An anti‑collision and damping system was developed, combining conductive contact detection with mechanical energy absorption to ensure safe operation. Validation through a dedicated mock‑up and experimental campaign confirmed the effectiveness of the approach. The architecture of the kinematic damping system, the mock-up design, and the results of the validation tests are presented here to provide a reference case for the design of next-generation instrumentation.

Items.Authors: Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: LOR mechanical design and analysis update
Items.Abstract: The LOR subsystem of MORFEO is approaching the Final Design Review (FDR). The mechanical design has now reached the final stage before procurement. In this presentation, the implemented mechanical solution, the simulations performed, and the methodology adopted to account for gravitational deformations and the vibration induced by the FREDA camera on the LOR board will be described.  The design of the LOR allows for an easy transition of the optical configuration from 1×1 to 2×2 on sky.

Items.Authors: Vincenzo De Caprio, Vincenzo Cianniello, Christian Eredia
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: mechanical design and subsystem interfaces improvement of the "Main Structure" from PDR to FDR
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. MORFEO has officially passed the Preliminary Design Review in February 2023 and it is entering the final design phase. The general overview of the mechanical design and subsystem interfaces for the Main Structure described in this paper is an improved configuration of the one presented at Preliminary Design Review in the first half of 2021.

Items.Authors: Federico Battaini, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Jacopo Farinato, Demetrio Magrin, Marco Riva, Daphne Diretto, Bernardo Salasnich, Giorgio Pariani, Matteo Munari
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: MiniTAC, a support equipment to test the LGSO focal and pupil planes
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.  MORFEO will include six laser guide stars wavefront sensors (LGS-WFS).  It is critical to test the optical quality of the beam delivered to the LGS WFS in terms of focal ratio, telecentricity, pupil distortion, and asterism delivery position. To this end, we present MiniTAC, a support equipment integrating three channels: a focal plane PSF imager, a pupil imaging system and a SH-WFS, mounted on motorized stages for field-of-view and axial scanning.

Items.Authors: Matteo D'Ambrogio, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Nicholas Devaney, Daphne Diretto, Bernardo Salasnich
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: optomechanical design of test alignment camera
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. The TAC (Test Alignment Camera) is a piece of equipment that will be installed inside the MES (MICADO Emulating Structure), under the LOR ( Low Order and Reference): its main function is to simulate and verify all the requirements regarding the interface between MORFEO and MICADO in the Bologna Integration Hall, before the whole system is sent to the ELT in Chile. The TAC is subdivided into Stage system, equipped with three linear stages – one for each axis – to precisely control the position of the assembly in space, and the Camera system, an aluminium plate housing sensors and the necessary optomechanics. This paper focuses on the optomechanical design of the TAC, presenting the overcome challenges and choices of equipment.

Items.Authors: Gabriele Rodeghiero, Benedetta Di Franceso, Ivan Di Antonio, Angelo Valentini, Gianluca Di Rico, Luca Rosignoli, Simone Benedetti, Amico Di Cianno, Mauro Dolci, Alexander Goncharov, Nicholas Devaney, Gabriele Umbriaco, Matteo Munari, Demetrio Magrin, Giorgio M. Pariani, Jacopo Farinato, Luca Marafatto, Alessandro Ballone, Lorenzo Busoni, Sylvain Oberti, Enrico Giro, Ludovico Teodori, Andrea Di Rocco, Paolo Ciliegi
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: paraxial calibration unit prototype alignment demonstration in the lab
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. The MORFEO calibration unit provides simultaneous natural and laser guide calibration sources to the multiple MORFEO wavefront sensors and the MICADO scientific field of view. The system adopts an optical design with many semi-reflective elements that leads to the presence of optical ghosts and an intrinsic low throughput. This work reports an empirical demonstration of the alignment strategy developed and tested exploiting a lab paraxial prototype.

Items.Authors: Gabriele Umbriaco, Diego Gilioli, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Sophie Antonia Penger, Luca Rosignoli, Alessio Taranto, Matteo Munari, Jacopo Farinato, Demetrio Magrin, Paolo Ciliegi
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: precision alignment of MORFEO’s laser guide star objective using MAT and PIP
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.   A Micro Alignment Telescope (MAT) equipped with a Point-Image-Point (PIP) system was used to validate a ghost-based optical alignment method for the MORFEO Laser Guide Star Objective (LGSO). Ghost reflections from optical surfaces were used as intrinsic references to define the optical axis without the need for external targets. Laboratory tests on a prototype, analyzed through MAT imaging and Python centroid routines, achieved residuals of 5 µm in decenter and 10 asec in tilt. Simulations applied to the LGSO–MORFEO model predict alignment errors of ~10 µm and 2 asec, one order of magnitude below system tolerances (1 mm, 360 asec). The MAT+PIP technique thus proves to be a compact, self-referenced, and highly precise tool for MORFEO alignment and integration.

Items.Authors: Jacopo Farinato, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Luca Marafatto, Gabriele Umbriaco, Marco Riva, Edoardo Redaelli, Demetrio Magrin, Vincenzo De Caprio, Vincenzo Cianniello, Giorgio Pariani, Matteo Munari, Matteo D'Ambrogio, Hossein Mahmoodzadeh, Matteo Aliverti, Sylvain Oberti, Lorenzo Busoni, Nicholas Devaney, Jean-Pierre Véran, Marco Bonaglia, Thibaut Moulin, Italo Foppiani, Simonetta Chinellato, Luca Rosignoli, Alessandro Ballone, Federico Battaini, Elena Carolo, Diego Gilioli, Giuseppe Di Luca, Simone Di Filippo, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Leonardo Buoncompagni, Alessio Taranto, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Andrea Baruffolo, Maria Bergomi, Giulio Capasso, Enrico Cascone, Manal Chebbo, Paolo Ciliegi, Mirko Colapietro, Elia Costa, Domenico D'Auria, Ivan Di Antonio, Benedetta Di Francesco, Chiara Di Prospero, Dafne Diretto, Gianluca Di Rico, Andrea Di Rocco, Mauro Dolci, Simone Doniselli, Christian Eredia, Enrico Giro, Alexander Goncharov, Laurent Jocou, Salvatore Lampitelli, Fulvio Laudisio, Alfio Puglisi, Bernardo Salasnich, Salvatore Savarese, Marcello Scalera, Mahshid Shiri, Rosanna Sordo, Ludovico Teodori, Angelo Valentini, Marco Xompero
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: the MAIT process in Europe, an update of the plan toward the instrument FDR
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For Elt Observations) is the post-focal AO module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). The main purpose of MORFEO is to relay the light beam from the ELT focal plane to the client instruments (MICADO and HARMONI) compensating, through a MCAO system, the atmospheric turbulence and other disturbances affecting the wavefronts of the scientific targets.  The optical design of the instrument has been conceived in a way that there are very relaxed alignment tolerances for all the optical components but a single compensator, the second spherical Deformable Mirror, which is actuated in tip-tilt and piston (through a hexapod system) to fine tune the optical quality provided to the client instruments. Additionally, two flat folding mirrors, motorized in Tip-Tilt and Piston, are used to properly position the pupil and focal plane on the client instruments.  In this paper we describe the AIT process that will be performed at INAF-OAS Bologna.

Items.Authors: Mirko Colapietro, Matteo Aliverti, Simone Doniselli, Bernardo Salasnich, Daphne Diretto
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: thermal control system manifold prototyping
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.   High thermal stability is critical for performance, necessitating a robust Thermal Control System (ThCS). This paper presents prototyping activities validating the ThCS architecture's ability to maintain temperature stability across MORFEO subsystems. We describe the thermal prototype design, including cooling strategies and control hardware selection. Performance tests characterized thermal response, controller performance, and system robustness under expected ELT operational conditions. Preliminary results confirm the prototype meets stability requirements, identifies critical interfaces, and guides design refinements. These activities significantly de-risk the final ThCS implementation, ensuring MORFEO's reliable telescope performance.

Items.Authors: Alessandro Ballone, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Demetrio Magrin, Jacopo Farinato, Leonardo Buoncompagni, Gabriele Umbriaco, Luca Rosignoli, Alessio Taranto, Davide Greggio, Luca Marafatto, Lorenzo Busoni, Giorgio Pariani, Matteo Munari, Elena Carolo, Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Federico Battaini, Simone Di Filippo, Matteo D'Ambrogio, Nicholas Devaney, Daphne Diretto, Fulvio Laudisio, Elia Costa, Bernardo Salasnich, Vincenzo Cianniello, Vincenzo De Caprio, Marco Riva, Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli, Ludovico Teodori, Andrea Di Rocco, Paolo Ciliegi
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: updates on the optical fine alignment strategy
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. Multiple MORFEO fine Optical Alignment strategies are currently under investigation. For this contribution, we report updates on the “Donut” method. In this approach, residual low order aberrations - due to misalignments - are estimated by calculating the moments of light in out-of-focus images on the instrumental focal plane detector. MORFEO’s M10, M11 and M12 can then be moved to compensate for those and align the pupil and focal planes between MORFEO and the attached instruments. We present several tests to assess the performances of this strategy, also accounting for stray light effects and demonstrating using more realistic “on-sky” donuts. This study is performed by means of sequential and non-sequential simulations with the Zemax software and its API.

Items.Authors: Meghna Mohamed, Alessandro Meoli, Walter Seifert, Andreas Kelz, Myriam Rodrigues, Alondra Solá, Wenli Xu, Carlos Rodriguez Alvarez, Gavin Dalton, Thomas Augusteijn, Kacem El Hadi, Marísa Luisa García-Vargas, Marie Larrieu, Roser Pello, Mathieu Puech, Rubén Sanchez-Janssen, Hermine Schnetler, Jay Stephan, Christian Surace
Items.Title: MOSAIC on ELT: VIS channel transmission budget and estimates – from system architecture review to preliminary design phase
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC for the 39 m ELT comes with MOS and mIFU capabilities in the wavelength range from 390 nm to 1800 nm and is currently in phase B2 leading up to PDR. The VIS Science Channel is intended to have separate low- and high-resolution fibre link feeds and a dual-beam two-camera design to split the spectrum (in blue and red arms), providing simultaneous coverage from 390 nm to 950 nm in low resolution and multiple high resolution bands in the same wavelength range. Transmission estimates of the VIS channel have helped in assessing potential risks in compliance and identifying the critical contributors impacting the transmission budget. This paper looks into VIS Channel transmission budget, the critical contributors impacting the transmission performance, and the evolution of the transmission estimates (and the methodology), from the System Architecture Review to the ongoing Preliminary Design phase.

Items.Authors: Dani Guzman, Nirmala Kunwar, Jake Linden, Cam Brown, Michael Boers, Jafar Shojaii, Mark Casali, Tayyaba Zafar, Benjamin Pope, Lee Spitler
Items.Title: MQ-Zero: Ultra-Compact Detector Controller for in-Vacuum FPA Readout
Items.Abstract: The Readout Sensors Initiative at Australian Astronomical Optics, Macquarie University, advances detector readout electronics for astronomy, space missions, and medical diagnostics. This paper presents MQ-Zero, a next-generation controller engineered for co-location with focal plane arrays in vacuum environments.    MQ Zero incorporates cutting-edge signal chain components while addressing vacuum system constraints. The ultra-compact form factor (70mm × 70mm) enables mosaic configurations for large focal planes. A key innovation is its thermal management strategy, extracting heat through conduction while preventing radiative loading of adjacent detectors.  On-board FPGA integration enables pixel processing, reducing data bandwidth and latency—advantageous for high-speed observations and space applications.    This paper details the design methodology, thermal analysis, signal chain optimization, and performance characterization, presenting results from a Test Board development and testing.

Items.Authors: Chiara D'Amato, Andrea Bianco, Giorgio Pariani, Fabrizio Fornasiero, Robert J. Harris, Sajjad Mahdizadeh, Sebastiaan Haffert, Aurelien Benoit, Viktoria Kutnohorsky, David MacLachlan, Tim Birks, Joss Guy, Robert R. Thomson, Jared R. Males, Laird M. Close, Olivier Guyon
Items.Title: Multi-Core Integral Field Unit (MCIFU v2): design and optimization of the integral field spectrograph with multiplexed VPH gratings
Items.Abstract: The Multi-Core Integral Field Unit (MCIFU v2) is a unit enabling infrared integral field spectroscopy for the MagAO-X adaptive optics system on the Magellan Clay telescope. Its fibre-fed integral field spectrograph was designed and optimized for exoplanet atmosphere characterization in the near-infrared. The design achieves diffraction-limited performance across the Y, J, and H bands with medium spectral resolution (R = 5000-7880), using a novel configuration of multiplexed volume phase holographic gratings and custom optics. The system was optimised with theoretical modelling in MATLAB and ray-tracing in Zemax OpticStudio, obtaining an improved set of lenses to control aberrations across the wide operating bandwidth. The final design achieves high diffraction efficiency (> 80%), low crosstalk (< 1%), and a compact configuration, making it a suitable candidate for future integration with the MagAO-X extreme adaptive optics system.

Items.Authors: Sajjad Mahdizadeh, Robert J. Harris, Aurélien Benoît, David MacLachlan, Tim Birks, Chiara D'Amato, Sebastiaan Haffert, Andrea Bianco, Joss Guy, Viktoria Kutnohorsky, Robert R. Thomson, Jared R. Males, Olivier Guyon, Laird M. Close
Items.Title: Multi-Core Integral Field Unit (MCIFU v2): fibre-link design and status
Items.Abstract: The Multi-Core Integral Field Unit (MCIFU v2) is an add-on for the MagAO-X adaptive optics system, enabling spectroscopy and spectral differential imaging of close companions such as protoplanets and exoplanets in the Y, J, and H bands at R~5000. MagAO-X provides a diffraction-limited focal plane, which the MCIFU samples using a 119-spaxel fibre link that relays a 1-arcsecond field-of-view to an external spectrograph. Two optimized fibre links are considered, one for Y+J (0.96–1.345 μm) and one for H (1.49–1.78 μm), each consisting of a Micro-Lens Array (MLA), a Multi-Core Fibre (MCF), and a photonic reformatter. A 3D-printed MLA enhances coupling into the MCF, whose Y+J design uses three dissimilar single-mode core types arranged to reduce crosstalk. At the output, an Ultrafast-Laser-Inscribed reformatter converts the hexagonal core layout into a linear slit with ~66% transmission and <5×10⁻⁴ crosstalk (simulation). The spectrograph then disperses all spaxels onto a HAWAII-2 detector.

Items.Authors: Philippe Voyer, Steven J. Benton, Benjamin E. Boyd, Aurélien A. Fraisse, Ajay S. Gill, Suren Gourapura, John W. Hartley, Bradley Holder, William C. Jones, Lun Li, Gavin Leroy, Thuy Vy T. Luu, Richard Massey, Jacqueline E. McCleary, Adyn Miles, Johanna M. Nagy, C. Barth Netterfield, Emaad Paracha, Susan F. Redmond, Jason D. Rhodes, L. Javier Romualdez, Sayan Saha, Jurgen Schmoll, Mohamed M. Shaaban, Simon Tartakovsky, Bryce J. Warren
Items.Title: Multi-sensor fusion for fine-guidance and milli-arcsecond-level attitude estimation of balloon-borne telescopes
Items.Abstract: Achieving sub-arcsecond pointing in the balloon environment requires precise attitude estimation despite structural vibrations, pendulation, and latency in optical measurements. This work evaluates a multi-sensor estimation framework for the Gigapixel Balloon-borne Imaging Telescope (GigaBIT), a 1.35-meter aperture instrument targeting 0.020 arcsec image stability during long-duration stratospheric flights. Using a nonlinear rigid-body model and sensor characteristics informed by prior SuperBIT missions, we simulate representative disturbance scenarios to assess performance. A bias-aware Multiplicative Extended Kalman Filter (MEKF) fuses gyro data with asynchronous vector measurements from focal-plane star cameras, and case studies explore the impact of latency, dropout, and multi-camera redundancy. Results guide GigaBIT’s flight software development and offer a generalizable approach for high-precision balloon-borne platforms.

Items.Authors: Michiel Darcis, Wilbert G. Ras-Vinke, Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Vincent Chambouleyron, Xavier Le Saux, David S. Doelman, Tonny Coppens, Dimitry Lamers, David Thoen, Matthew A. Kenworthy, Pieter J. de Visser
Items.Title: Multi-wavelength wavefront reconstruction with the Zernike wavefront sensor and MKIDs
Items.Abstract: Future high-contrast imaging instruments require highly precise wavefront sensing. A promising way to improve wavefront sensors is to utilize currently under-exploited wavelength information through new developments such as Microwave Kinetic Inductance Detectors (MKIDs) and semi-analytical gradient descent reconstructors. This work starts with examining the advantages of using multi-wavelength reconstruction for the Zernike Wavefront Sensor (ZWFS). Using numerical simulations, the improvements in dynamic range, photon noise sensitivity and phase unwrapping are investigated. A testbed has been setup to test the multi-wavelength reconstruction together with a 400 pixel MKID. Using a blue and red laser simultaneously, Zernike aberrations are reconstructed using the stream of photon pulses coming from the MKID. These results are compared to those obtained from a CMOS camera with separate blue and red images. The dynamic range extension using multi-wavelength measurements is demonstrated.

Items.Authors: Takeshi Nakazato, Hajime Ezawa, Kanako Sugimoto, Karl Torstensson, Andres Guzman, Laura Gómez, Kotomi Taniguchi, Akira Yoshino, Ihor Ihnatiev
Items.Title: New geometrical algorithm for the ALMA Single-Dish Pipeline to identify pointing outlier data and its impact on the ALMA operation
Items.Abstract: Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) delivers reduced and quality assessed data to users. In ALMA, control software of the antenna excludes data when antenna pointing deviates from predefined trajectory. However, there are several cases that single-dish data associated with deviant antenna pointing were not excluded properly. To overcome this issue, we developed generic geometrical algorithm that works without knowing the extent of the observing region specified by the user. For On-the-Fly raster scan data, median separation of the antenna pointings from the nominal center of the observation can be used to estimate the size of the observing area even if outlier data exist. ALMA Single-Dish Pipeline with the new algorithm excluded pointing outlier from the processing as expected. This improvement almost eliminated an extra effort to reprocess the data with pointing outlier. The algorithm may have possible applications to other areas requiring outlier detection.

Items.Authors: Simone Lotti, Francesco Monastra, Giacomo Gorla, Matteo D'Andrea, Nicolina Chrysaphi, Monica Laurenza, Claudio Macculi, Luigi Piro
Items.Title: NewAthena X-IFU non–X-ray background: Geant4 simulations, veto optimization, and laboratory validation
Items.Abstract: We report on Geant4 simulations of the non–X-ray background (NXB) for the NewAthena X-IFU, focusing on updated mass models, veto strategies, and validation.   The mass model evolved with mission redefinition, including a new cryostat and focal plane assembly, L-grooves, and absorber layouts. High-statistics simulations show modest changes in background relative to the 2017 model, and confirm spatial homogeneity. Although the design is not yet finalized in all its elements, the results’ representativeness increased with respect to previous results.  A sector veto strategy exploiting CryoAC segmentation can keep 75% of the TES array active, raising NXB by ~50%; extending the veto region by Δ pixels reduces the increment to 6% for Δ=5.   A preliminary solar energetic particle simulation confirmed background levels exceeding requirements by three orders of magnitude. Validation against CryoAC prototype data demonstrated strong agreement, supporting the robustness of the simulation framework.

Items.Authors: Katelyn A. Horstman, Charles Beichman, David Ciardi, Jinhao Ge, Stehanie Leifer, Luke Finnerty, Greg Doppmann, Daniel Echeverri, Ben Sappey, Elijah Anakalea-Buckley, Jean-Baptiste Ruffio, Chih-Chun Hsu, Dimitri Mawet, Nemanja Jovanovic
Items.Title: NIR laser frequency comb integration with Keck Planet Imager and Characterizer (KPIC)
Items.Abstract: Laser Frequency Combs (LFCs) are essential calibration units for spectrographs that specialize in precision and extreme precision radial velocity (PRV/EPRV) measurements to search for planets around stellar hosts. They create a spectrum of discrete and regularly spaced frequencies used to derive wavelength solutions during the data reduction process. Recently, the Keck Planet Imager and Characterizer (KPIC), a fiber injection unit that feeds the high resolution spectrograph NIRSPEC (R~35,000) at the W.M. Keck Observatory, has successfully integrated a specially built, near-infrared LFC into its optical system for H-band (1.5-1.8 microns) observations. We present the ability of the LFC to correct drifts within the NIRSPEC spectrograph, the derivation of the wavelength solution using the LFC, and on-sky observations of TOI-1531, a binary system with a close-in stellar companion found from high resolution imaging with a Neptune-sized, transiting planetary candidate discovered by TESS.

Items.Authors: Juan Carlos Guerra, Sam Ragland, Brandon Mechtley
Items.Title: Non-invasive optical gain estimation in pyramid wavefront sensors from telemetry using machine learning
Items.Abstract: The optical gain of the pyramid wavefront sensor varies with atmospheric turbulence parameters such as seeing and coherence time directly influencing the accuracy of adaptive optics (AO) corrections. At the Large Binocular Telescope Observatory (LBTO), gain is tracked using a probe signal injected into the AO loop, which has minimal impact on most science observations but can interfere with advanced second generation instruments.   Leveraging archived AO telemetry, we integrate optical gain (Gopt) into a machine learning (ML) framework to predict its behavior as a non invasive alternative to probe injection. Preliminary analysis reveals a strong correlation of −78% between seeing and Gopt, motivating the use of Random Forest regression and Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) networks. Our results demonstrate that ML based Gopt prediction achieves reliable accuracy, enabling smoother AO operations and the overall operational efficiency under highly variable atmospheric conditions.

Items.Authors: Uma Subash, Hanshin Lee
Items.Title: Numerical modeling and performance prediction of the Hobby Eberly Telescope’s new Edge Sensor system
Items.Abstract: The current inductive edge sensor used in the Segment Alignment Maintenance System (SAMS) of the Hobby Eberly Telescope maintains and corrects thermally induced misalignments in 91 segments of the primary mirror. This old SAMS is getting upgraded to a retroreflector–collimator-based edge sensor. This work presents a numerical model of the new SAMS and its role in dynamic alignment maintenance. The system uses laser distance interferometry to measure changes in channel lengths and estimate segment misalignments, enabling corrections in focus, tip, and tilt. A minimal PID control loop optimizes dynamic alignment control under varying temperature conditions. Case studies using real temperature-time profiles show that the model maintains tip and tilt within 0.1 arcsec 50% of the time and 0.3 arcsec 90% of the time.

Items.Authors: Alejandro Buendía-Roca, Nazim Ali Bharmal, Carlos González-Gutiérrez, Saúl Pérez-Fernández, Juan Antonio de Abol-Blasón, Santiago Iglesias-Álvarez, Julía Fernández Díaz, Fernando Sánchez Lasheras, Francisco Javier de Cos Juez
Items.Title: Off-axis atmospheric turbulence reconstruction with WOMBAT
Items.Abstract: We present a study of off-axis adaptive optics performance using WOMBAT, a system that projects an expanded laser beam through the telescope pupil to sample atmospheric turbulence across multiple directions. Neural networks are trained to reconstruct the three-dimensional turbulence from the beam image. In this work, we quantify how prediction accuracy degrades with increasing angular separation from the telescope axis and identify the main sources of off-axis error. The results outline the practical limits of WOMBAT and the conditions under which neural-network tomography remains reliable for wide-field AO applications.

Items.Authors: Juhyeong Kim, Dae-Hee Lee, Chae Kyung Sim
Items.Title: Onboard AI for space exploration: from Raspberry Pi validation to a mission-suitable model
Items.Abstract: Planetary exploration missions face inevitable limitations such as communication delays and limited downlink capacity. Onboard AI is a possible solution for autonomous data analysis and improved communication efficiency. However, a conventional GPU-based AI system is unsuitable for space due to high power consumption and vulnerability to radiation and extreme temperatures.  To address this, we target a lightweight, low-power AI system designed for onboard operation. As an initial step, we demonstrated real-time object detection on Raspberry Pi 4B using YOLOv5n. It consumed a few watts of power, confirming the feasibility of embedded AI for spacecraft platforms. Then we adapted the model to be suitable for spacecraft imaging instruments by enabling it to directly process raw, intensity-only data. The revised model showed improved accuracy and speed. Also, we are developing a lightweight super-resolution model and planning FPGA implementation for future space-qualified deployment.

Items.Authors: Narsireddy Anugu, John D. Monnier, Stefan Kraus, Robert Klement, Gail H. Schaefer, Douglas R. Gies
Items.Title: On-sky demonstration of dual-field interferometry at the CHARA Array
Items.Abstract: We report an on-sky demonstration of dual-field interferometry at the CHARA Array, a capability inspired by the dual-beam architecture of VLTI/GRAVITY and designed to expand CHARA’s sensitivity, astrometric precision, and scientific reach. Our approach uses MIRC-X (H-band) and MYSTIC (K-band) beam combiners in a paired configuration, where one instrument operates as a real-time fringe tracker while the other records long-exposure science fringes on a second target within the 5″ interferometric field of view. The roles of the two instruments are interchangeable, enabling dual-field operation across a wide wavelength range J/H/K. Dual-field fringes were first obtained in summer 2025 on the bright wide binary α Piscium, marking the first demonstration of off-axis fringe tracking at CHARA. Our goals include extending this mode to faint-target interferometry, enabling long-exposure coherent integrations on stars several magnitudes fainter than the real-time fringe-tracking limit.

Items.Authors: Petr Janout, Julienne Böttger, Felipe Pedreros Bustos, Deborah Malone, Samuel Lévêque
Items.Title: On-sky detection of discontinued phase with laser guide star
Items.Abstract: As next-generation large-aperture telescopes adopt segmented primary mirrors, precise co-phasing of segments to well below the observing wavelength is critical for diffraction-limited performance. Residual piston, tip, or tilt between segments introduces phase discontinuities that degrade the point-spread function and overall image quality. We extend previous work on detecting discontinuous optical phase steps and demonstrate on-sky measurement using the CaNaPy facility. CaNaPy, a laser guide star adaptive optics platform for visible wavelengths, enables evaluation under realistic turbulence and adverse conditions. Three precision-fabricated transmissive phase masks simulate segment discontinuities, and the resulting wavefronts are measured with a pyramid piston sensor under various conditions, with and without AO correction. The outcomes of these experiments will inform future on-sky alignment strategies for segmented mirrors.

Items.Authors: Nathan Leguay, Jean Fontignie, Christophe Cara, Grégory Kaszubiak, Thomas Capocci, Cyrille Delisle, Léna Provost, Duc-Dat Huynh, Michel Berthé, Pierre Garcia, Gaël Vignon, Pascale Danto, Hervé Fossecave, Gaëlle Giesen, Elodie Jacquel, Marta Rizzo, François Nouals, Benoît Horeau, Isabelle Le Mer, Jérôme Martignac, François Visticot, Diana Renaud, Marion Baumann, Manuel Morales, Leo Farhat, Marie-Genevieve Perichaud, Ludovic Puig, Alina Spuma, Enrique Cordero
Items.Title: Operational amplifier's behavior at cryo temperatures: the case of ARIEL AIRS cold front-end electronics
Items.Abstract: In a few years, the ARIEL space telescope will study the atmosphere of hundreds of exoplanets through the ARIEL Infra-Red Spectrometer (AIRS) developed by a French consortium of laboratories.    The AIRS instrument is composed of two detector control unit (DCU) located in the service module of the satellite driving two integrated focal plane assembly (iFPA), which operates at cryo temperatures in the payload module. Right behind the detectors, cold front-end electronics (CFEE) are in charge of amplifying the signals to decrease their susceptibility to external noises through their way to the DCU located in the service module. Thus, French teams needed to find a very low-noise amplifier that could operate at temperatures down to 37K, in the harsh space environment.    This paper will first present the issue encountered with the initial selection (OPA2350) and more extensively describe the results of the long test campaign organized to validate the selection of the OP2192.

Items.Authors: Luca Oggioni, Fabrizio Fornasiero, Giorgio M. Pariani, Samuel Ronayette
Items.Title: Optical design and analysis of the InfraRed Telescope (IRT) for the ESA THESEUS Mission
Items.Abstract: The InfraRed Telescope (IRT) of the ESA THESEUS mission is a 0.7m off-axis three-mirror anastigmat optimized for imaging and spectroscopy in the 0.7–1.8 µm range to enable rapid GRB follow-up. We present the optical design and performance analysis of the M7 baseline. The system achieves diffraction-limited quality across both photometric and spectroscopic fields, as demonstrated by EE, spot quality and MTF results. A comprehensive Monte-Carlo tolerance analysis, including manufacturing, alignment and stability, defines feasible tolerances and compensator strategies that keep EED50/EED80 within requirements.

Items.Authors: Olivier Lardière, Christian Marois, Adam Johnson, Joeleff Fitzsimmons
Items.Title: Optical design and assembly of CAL2: the NRC Canada facility-class focal plane wavefront sensor for the Gemini Planet Imager 2 upgrade
Items.Abstract: The Calibration 2 (CAL2) system, being built by NRC-Herzberg with Canadian and international collaborators, is a facility-class focal plane wavefront sensor for the Gemini Planet Imager 2 (GPI2) upgrade, scheduled to be delivered in the Spring of 2026. CAL2 is a complete rebuild of the GPI CAL system. The goal of CAL2 is to replace the dual-arm interferometer by a single-arm all-refractive interferometer, much less sensitive to vibration. CAL2 is based on a self-coherent camera and a Tilt-Gaussian focal plane mask boosting the reference beam and enabling high-speed coherent differential imaging (CDI) and active speckle nulling using GPI deformable mirror. CAL2 should improve GPI contrast by a factor 100 on bright stars. We are presenting here the optical design, the assembly and alignment processes as well as the test results.

Items.Authors: Nicolò Azzaroli, Cédric Plantet, Fernando Quirós-Pacheco, Bo Xin, Arielle Bertrou-Cantou, Gary Muller, Juan Pablo Haddad, Brian McLeod, Jan Kansky, Simone Esposito, Richard Demers
Items.Title: Optical design of the GMT Adaptive optics and Phasing Sensors (GAPS) testbed
Items.Abstract: The Giant Magellan Telescope (GMT) Adaptive Optics and Phasing Sensors (GAPS) testbed is designed to validate key elements of the GMT Natural Guide Star AO control system. This paper presents its optical design. The setup uses a seven-segment mirror to replicate the GMT’s segmented pupil and introduce phasing errors, while a 2k-actuator deformable mirror provides atmospheric turbulence injection, high-order correction, and compensation of minor optical aberrations. The testbed hosts the NGWS prototype, combining a high-order Pyramid WFS with the Hologram Dispersed Fringe Sensor (HDFS), essential for robust measurement of large differential piston between segments. This dual-sensor architecture enables realistic testing and refinement of the GMT NGAO control loop, demonstrating high-order correction and reliable segment phasing.

Items.Authors: Aashay Pai, Alex Drlica-Wagner, Lee S. Kelvin, Joshua E. Meyers
Items.Title: Optical ghosts: quantifying their impact and using them to probe LSSTCam optics
Items.Abstract: The Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) will reach an r-band coadded depth of 27.5 mag, enabling a surface brightness limit of > 30 mags per square arcsec. Such science demands careful control of systematics, including optical ghosts, which are artifacts caused by reflections between lenses, filters, and detectors. These features are unavoidable due to non-zero reflectances of the refractive optical elements and pose a challenge for low-surface-brightness measurements. Using optical ray-tracing simulations calibrated to LSST commissioning data, we define the ‘impacted area’ as regions where ghost surface brightness exceeds one-third of the sky noise. We find that, under a wide-fast-deep–like strategy, ~0.57% of the LSSTCam focal plane is affected when averaged across all bands. We also use ghost measurements to constrain the reflectances of LSSTCam optical elements.

Items.Authors: Scott O. Rohrbach, Alejandro S. Borlaff
Items.Title: Optical modeling for better on-orbit stray light background subtraction in the Roman Space Telescope Wide Field Instrument
Items.Abstract: The stray-light that a telescope receives from a contaminating source is described by the Normalized Detector Irradiance (NDI) function. NDI defines how much stray-light background will be seen at any point in the detector space from any (or every) source in the sky. NDI depends on the angular distance (R), position (roll, ϕ) angle of the source with respect of the detector axes and for especially wide field instruments like WFI, can vary widely as a function of position at the focal plane. Convolving the NDI with the position and flux of nearby stars directly provides a stray-light background correction.  We present the optical model and ray trace results being used to generate a high-resolution NDI maps for the Nancy Grace Roman Wide Field Instrument, and describe the dominant scattering features associated with the structure seen in the NDI maps. These optical models are the core of ROSALIA (ROman Sky Analyst for Low surface brightness Imaging & Astronomy)

Items.Authors: Anne-Sophie Poulin-Girard, Nathalie Blanchard, Alexandre Chevrette, Martin Larouche
Items.Title: Optical performance evaluation and end-to-end simulation of a 20cm compact space telescope for precision photometry
Items.Abstract: Precision photometry enables applications such as exoplanet detection, stellar variability studies, asteroid characterization, and space surveillance of Resident Space Objects (RSOs). Space-based instruments provide advantages over ground systems, including continuous observation, improved precision, and access to blocked spectral bands. We present optical performance and task-based simulations for a compact 20 cm VIS-NIR Three-Mirror Anastigmat telescope with a COTS CMOS detector. Metrics such as SNR for faint targets, PSF FWHM variation with object distance, photometric accuracy, and centroid stability are assessed. Monte Carlo tolerancing offers statistical insight into optical performance and supports integration and alignment strategies.

Items.Authors: Isabel J. Kain, Renate Kupke, Daren Dillon, R. Deno Stelter, Rosalie McGurk, Marc Kassis, Scott Lilley, Peyton Benac, Mackenzie Lach, Arun Surya, Amirul Hasan, Ravinder Banyal, Raquel Martinez, Athira Unni, Nicholas MacDonald, William Deich, Aaron Hunter, Emily Plume, Michael Gonzales, Cristian Rodriguez, Gwendolin Weber-Stover, Arjun Kumar, Cyril Bourgenot, Paul White, Jürgen Schmoll, James T. Wells, Spencer Davies, David Bramall, Dimitri Mawet, Olivier Absil, Michael Fitzgerald, Eric Wang, Steph Sallum, Andy Skemer
Items.Title: Optical performance of SCALES
Items.Abstract: The Slicer Combined with an Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy (SCALES) instrument is a 1-5µm imager and 2-5µm integral field spectrograph, currently being commissioned on the Keck II Telescope. SCALES is optimized for exoplanet high-contrast imaging and spectroscopic characterization, and will be sensitive to older, colder exoplanets than existing instrumentation. The 12.3”x 12.3” imaging channel is designed to replicate the capabilities of NIRC2, and the low (R∼35-250, 2.2”x2.2” FOV) and medium (R∼3500-7000, 0.36”x0.34” FOV) spectral resolution modes offer new capabilities compared to existing Keck instrumentation. We present preliminary optical performance results from laboratory testing and commissioning of SCALES.

Items.Authors: Salvador Cuevas Cardona, Luis C. Alvarez Nuñez, Rubén Flores-Meza, Beatriz Sánchez , Leonardo Garcés Medina, Oscar Chapa Hernandez, Carolina Keiman, Gerardo Lara Lucario, Carlos Espejo
Items.Title: Optical quality tests in Imaging and IFS modes of the GTC/FRIDA instrument in the laboratory
Items.Abstract: We describe the optical quality tests of GTC/FRIDA at the UNAM in Mexico before the GTC engineers’ acceptance in the laboratory. We expect to send FRIDA to La Palma in 2026. FRIDA is an imager and integral field spectrograph (IFS) that will operate in the near-infrared (0.9-2.5m) with the corrected beam provided by GTCAO, the adaptive optics (AO) system of GTC. FRIDA performs the imaging and IFS modes with only an H2RG detector. The instrument provides three pixel/spaxel scales: 10, 20, and 40 mas by means of three cameras. In its IFS mode FRIDA performs a slicer Integral Field Unit with 30 slices and it features two resolutions: (i) medium (R1500-4000) in the z, J ,H, K bands and (ii) high (R30000) in H and K bands. Additionally, FRIDA exhibits high-contrast capabilities with the presence of classical Lyot coronagraphs in both imaging and IFS.

Items.Authors: Akhil Mahesh, Michael D. Audley, Pieter Dieleman, Ilija Lichkovski, Dmitry Orlov, Emilie Kernen, Heino P. Smit, Willem-Jan Vreeling
Items.Title: Optically stimulated luminescence as the origin of the post-pulse tail of the in-flight calibration sources for X-IFU
Items.Abstract: Modulated x-ray sources (MXSs) have been used for the in-flight calibration of the Hitomi and XRISM x-ray missions and will be used for NewAthena’s X-IFU. Their principle of operation is the (pulsed) modulation of an LED that stimulates the emission of electrons from the photocathode, which are accelerated by high voltage to the anode target, emitting x-rays. It is known that the MXSs produce a post-pulse decaying tail of x-ray emission of unconfirmed origin, whose intensity decreases relative to the x-ray pulse intensity as the photocathode ages. A lifetime test of an MXS was performed, during which measurements were made that show the tail has a dependence on the wavelength and intensity of the stimulation light, independent of the x-ray pulse intensity. We propose that optically stimulated luminescence in the materials of the MXSs explains the tail’s behaviour.

Items.Authors: Raveena Koliyatan Manamparambil, Nicholas Devaney
Items.Title: Optimizing the performance of holographic wavefront sensor using computer generated holograms
Items.Abstract: This presentation explores how holographic wavefront sensing can improve the performance of adaptive optical systems used in astronomy. We examine how design choices affect measurement accuracy and discuss strategies for optimizing sensor performance.

Items.Authors: Tanmoy Chattopadhyay, Sven Herrmann, Kevan Donlon, Ilya Prigozhin, Peter Orel, Steven W. Allen, Marshall W. Bautz, Michael Cooper, Catherine E. Grant, Beverly J. LaMarr, Christopher Leitz, Eric D. Miller, Glenn Morris, Abigail Y. Pan, Tonya Peshel, Artem Poliszczuk, Gregory Prigozhin, Haley R. Stueber, Keith Warner
Items.Title: Output-stage design optimization for high-sensitivity SiSeRO-CCDs and SiSeRO active pixel sensors
Items.Abstract: Single electron Sensitive Read Out (SiSeRO) is a new device class for next-generation astronomical X-ray telescopes requiring fast, low-noise, megapixel spectro-imagers and other applications that require sub-electron noise detectors. With the first-generation SiSeRO-CCD prototypes, we achieved a read noise level of around 3.5 electrons in single read mode (625 kpix/sec) and a sub-electron noise performance of 0.51 electrons in Repetitive Non-Destructive Readout mode at an impressive readout speed of 10 kpix/sec. For further maturation of the SiSeRO technology we initiated device simulations of the output stage, in particular, optimization of the sensing transistor and its internal gate geometry to enhance the noise and speed performance. We are also exploring output stage design options to develop a SiSeRO active pixel sensor (APS) matrix. We discuss our device simulation framework and validation using laboratory results from the first-generation SiSeRO devices.
